name: Zilpah
overview: Zilpah was a female servant of Leah who was given to her and later became a wife of Jacob. She played a significant role as a concubine in the family of Jacob, contributing to the growth of Leah's children through her. Her position is noted in the early Genesis narrative concerning the patriarchal family.
namesAndTitles: The name Zilpah means 'short nosed person' according to the Hebrew origin noted in Genesis 29:24. This is the only recorded name for her and does not carry a divine or special title.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Zilpah as the servant of Leah and the wife of Jacob. She is also the mother of Gad and Asher, two of Jacob's sons who became heads of tribes in Israel. These relationships are explicitly and implicitly documented in Genesis 29:24 and Genesis 30:9-13.
scriptureSignificance: Zilpah's importance lies in her role as a servant given to Leah who, through her union with Jacob, bore two sons. These sons, Gad and Asher, became progenitors of two of the twelve tribes of Israel, thus playing a foundational role in the establishment of Israel's tribal structure. Her story highlights God's providence in continuing the lineage of Jacob through various family arrangements.
